title: Reading in Depth: Taking a Book Apart with Notes
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: When you read a book, do you read it, or do you take it apart?

groups.heading: What it means to take a book apart

lines.text: Taking a book apart means reading for the decisions the author makes and the tension around them, and taking notes as you go, not only following the story.

What is important in this chapter is how the author is growing his business, the decisions the author is making, and the tension the author has with people. The author is transforming the whole business model.
I asked the group how the pace was and whether they were enjoying the book.
A student said: it was their second time reading it, and they were getting way more out of it this time.

This is how I read a book. I read it very in depth. I analyze a lot of things and I take a lot of notes. Even when I like a movie, I print the script and read it, because I absorb a lot more reading it than watching.
I have at least twenty or thirty really good books that I believe are life-changing for business and personal life.

Later we can read something more technical, like venture capital books about how small companies are structured and capitalized. But I like that we are reading a narrative, a story first. Then when we get into the technical, you will have a background.

groups.heading: One example: the author's way of seeing

lines.text: Think about billboards. A picture, an image, is a form of content. Radio is content too, just voice. But I think the author didn't really get into the voice. The author wanted something visual, because coming from billboards it was all about the visual.
I think the author has a visual intelligence. The way the author describes his sailing, you see pictures when he talks. I think that is why the author wanted to go right to television.

One question to ask when you take a book apart: what might explain the choices the author makes? In this example, Jose infers that the author's way of seeing in pictures may be why the author went straight to television.
The technical, believe it or not, is a lot easier than people think. Colleges make it more difficult than it really is.
How do you read the things that matter to you?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write one book or article you want to take apart, not just read.
Write how you will take notes: margins, a notebook, a printed copy.
Write one idea from it you will test this week.
Write a story that taught you something before you learned the technical side.
Write one thing that seems hard that might be easier than people say.

check.q: A reader wants to take a chapter apart, not just read it. What should they look for first?
choices: The length of the chapter and where it falls in the book
The decisions the author makes and the tension around them
How often the author repeats the same words in the chapter
Which parts of the chapter can be skipped to save time

check.q: In the lesson, what does Jose infer from the author's way of seeing in pictures?
choices: That a person's training matters more than their strengths
That the author's choices cannot be explained at all
That it may explain why the author went straight to television
That pictures are a weaker kind of content than voice

check.q: Why does the lesson prefer to read a story before the technical material?
choices: The story gives a background for the technical part
The technical material is not needed once the story is read
The story is shorter and quicker to get through in a sitting
The technical material should be read first, before the story

recap: Take a book apart: read for the author's decisions and tension, and take notes. Learn the story first, then the technical part.
